selected.lesson_subject: Seven-day setup period: cumulative uptime, FortiCare registration enforcement, and offline hardware registration
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiOS 8.0 newer hardware starts a seven-day cumulative powered-on setup window at first power-up; GUI/CLI access is available during the window, countdown pauses only when logged out and powered off, and FortiCare registration ends the window early; expiration gates management access until registration.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: First power-on -> first GUI/CLI login -> registration prompt/postpone -> cumulative uptime decrements while powered on and logged in -> register with FortiCare or upload offline license file -> management access remains available; after expiry, register or use offline registration recovery.
selected.failure_class: Management lockout after unregistered setup window; air-gapped hardware unable to reach FortiCare; wrong assumption that FortiGate-VM follows hardware offline-license workflow.
selected.evidence_pattern: FortiOS setup dialog and remaining uptime; device registration state; GUI/CLI access warning; FortiCare asset registration and downloaded offline license; `show full sys fortiguard` validates FortiGuard configuration but does not prove FortiCare registration succeeded.
selected.remediation_path: Before staging, confirm model/BIOS/FortiOS applicability and network reachability; for isolated hardware pre-register asset and stage the offline license file; if the grace period has elapsed, use supported factory reset/recovery and upload the off-network license, then validate FortiGuard settings; do not apply hardware workflow to FortiGate-VM.
selected.question_fingerprint: Distinguish cumulative powered-on setup time from wall-clock time; determine which event pauses or ends the timer; select the correct offline hardware versus VM recovery path.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Lifecycle timeline: first power-on -> login/postpone -> cumulative uptime gate -> FortiCare online or offline license branch -> GUI/CLI enabled; side callout for hardware-only applicability and VM exception.

selected.lesson_subject: PDE-aware import of password-type objects from managed FortiGates
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiManager 8.0.0 imports objects containing password-type attributes from FortiGates with private data encryption enabled; the Import Wizard requires an administrator-supplied password for new password-bearing objects and offers a preserve-current-password path for objects already present in the ADOM.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Managed FortiGate object database -> import wizard reads object metadata and encrypted password attributes -> administrator supplies password for new objects or chooses blank to retain the existing FortiGate password -> imported object becomes ADOM-managed -> subsequent installation resolves device mappings and deploys references.
selected.failure_class: Import fails or creates unusable credentials when PDE password material is not supplied or mismatched; inadvertent credential replacement when existing object password is re-entered incorrectly; confusion between object import and policy installation.
selected.evidence_pattern: Import Wizard explicitly lists password-bearing objects and prompts for secret material; successful object appears in ADOM object database; installation preview and device-side object validation show whether the object is deployable; import success alone does not prove downstream authentication works.
selected.remediation_path: Confirm FortiManager 8.0 compatibility and PDE state; import in a controlled ADOM; use the correct password for new objects; leave the field blank only when intentionally preserving the password already held by the FortiGate; validate object mapping and a controlled install, then test the dependent service.
selected.question_fingerprint: Choose the correct wizard action for a new password-bearing object versus an existing ADOM object; distinguish import-time secret handling from later installation mapping.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Two-lane object-import sequence: FortiGate/PDE source -> Import Wizard -> new-object password prompt or existing-object preserve-password branch -> ADOM object store -> install preview -> managed device.

selected.lesson_subject: FortiAnalyzer 8.0 playbook editor: node-level debugging, replay, partial runs, and Jinja control flow
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAnalyzer 8.0 playbook editor adds step-by-step execution that can run, pause, and inspect each task node; replay with alternate inputs; partial execution from a selected node; Branch/Wait/Compare/Switch control operators; and Jinja expressions for conditions and loops.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Trigger/input -> connector task -> node input/output context -> execute prior task to seed current task -> inspect task output -> pause/stop/delete/skip -> replay workflow with test data or restart from selected node -> full workflow execution after validation.
selected.failure_class: Playbook branch or connector failure hidden by whole-workflow execution; stale input or inactive connector mistaken for logic defect; rerunning all side effects during testing; Jinja condition/loop mis-evaluation.
selected.evidence_pattern: Per-node input/output panes and task execution status prove a task ran with the displayed input; replay proves behavior for that test payload only; partial run proves downstream nodes from a selected point but does not validate upstream trigger or connector state; connector grayed-out state indicates inactive/unconfigured connector.
selected.remediation_path: Validate trigger and connector readiness first; execute one node at a time; inspect the prior node output and current node input; replay with representative payloads; use partial runs only after upstream data is known-good; add Branch/Wait/Compare/Switch and Jinja incrementally, then run the full playbook with safe test targets.
selected.question_fingerprint: Differentiate node-level debugging, replay, and partial run; infer what each execution mode does and does not validate.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Playbook graph with trigger, connector nodes, Branch/Wait/Compare/Switch branches, node-level input/output inspection, replay loop, and partial-run entry point.

selected.lesson_subject: Media Redundancy Protocol ring manager/client election, ring-check frames, and two-ring constraints
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSwitch MRP forms an Ethernet ring with one manager/automanager and client nodes; ring ports are physical or one static trunk and are excluded from STP; manager election uses numerically lower priority then lowest MAC; MRP_Test, MRP_LinkChange, and MRP_TopologyChange frames drive failure/recovery state; 7.6+ supports two rings and ring-check mode but not MIM/MIC.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Configure identical MRP domain/VLAN/profile on all nodes -> manager/client roles and ring ports established -> manager monitors MRP_Test frames -> link failure produces LinkChange/TopologyChange -> manager opens the ring path -> link recovery re-evaluates ring closure; two-ring deployments require unique domain/port identifiers per ring.
selected.failure_class: Ring remains disabled due to MRP VLAN not allowed/native on both ring ports; inconsistent domain ID or profile; manager conflict; ring ports also participating in STP; unsupported MIM/MIC topology.
selected.evidence_pattern: MRP status and role/port state show control-plane agreement; MRP_Test/LinkChange/TopologyChange frames prove ring protocol signaling; link-state recovery and traffic continuity prove forwarding recovery; they do not prove application-level convergence or unsupported interconnection behavior.
selected.remediation_path: Check feature-matrix support; ensure ring VLAN is allowed/native on both ports on every node; align domain ID/profile; configure either one manager or automanager election consistently; remove ring ports from STP; verify two-ring unique IDs and keep unsupported MIM/MIC out of design.
selected.question_fingerprint: Identify manager election tie-breaks, distinguish the three MRP frame types, and diagnose a ring disabled by VLAN mismatch versus manager conflict.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Physical Ethernet ring with one manager, multiple clients, two ring ports per node, blocked STP participation, MRP control frames, and a second-ring inset showing unique domain/port IDs.

selected.lesson_subject: WPA3 Beacon Protection: beacon-frame integrity, PMF dependency, and VAP-level enablement
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Beacon Protection adds integrity protection to beacon management frames on WPA3 SSIDs; it is configured per VAP, disabled by default, and supported on FortiAP Wi-Fi 6E/7 models running FAP 7.6.1 or later; Protected Management Frames must be enabled.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Client scans -> AP advertises WPA3 SSID and beacon-protection capability -> AP emits integrity-protected beacon -> compatible client validates beacon integrity before trusting discovery/association information -> client proceeds with WPA3/PMF association.
selected.failure_class: Feature configured on unsupported AP/firmware; beacon protection enabled without PMF/WPA3 prerequisites; legacy client cannot join or ignores protected beacon behavior; VAP profile not actually bound to serving radio.
selected.evidence_pattern: VAP configuration shows WPA3 security, PMF enabled, and beacon-protection enabled; AP profile/radio binding proves the setting is applied to the intended SSID; over-the-air capture shows protected beacon integrity fields; successful association alone does not prove every nearby client validates the protected beacon.
selected.remediation_path: Confirm Wi-Fi 6E/7 model and FAP 7.6.1+; configure WPA3 and PMF on the VAP before enabling beacon protection; bind the VAP to the correct AP profile/radio; validate with a compatible client and packet capture; retain a separate legacy SSID if older clients cannot support WPA3/PMF.
selected.question_fingerprint: Select the correct prerequisites and distinguish beacon-frame integrity protection from data-frame encryption, PMF generally, or MLO.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: VAP-to-radio binding diagram plus 802.11 discovery sequence: beacon capability advertisement, integrity-protected beacon, client validation, WPA3/PMF association.

selected.lesson_subject: Access Point Management: DHCP lease validation and StaticIPAddress enforcement for clients behind non-VLAN-aware APs
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC Access Point Management controls hosts behind access points/hubs that cannot enforce per-client VLANs by validating each host MAC against FortiNAC-maintained DHCP lease state; absent MAC/IP lease creates a StaticIPAddress event that can map to an alarm and action.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: AP/hub forwards client traffic on shared network -> FortiNAC DHCP view allocates/records authorized lease and DNS behavior -> host connects -> FortiNAC checks host MAC in DHCP lease file -> valid lease permits production access; missing lease emits StaticIPAddress event -> alarm mapping triggers configured host action.
selected.failure_class: Static-IP endpoint bypasses DHCP lease evidence; DHCP relay/scope or lease file is missing; alarm event is generated but not mapped to an action; non-VLAN-aware AP cannot isolate a single client with VLAN assignment.
selected.evidence_pattern: DHCP lease file contains MAC/IP/VLAN mapping; StaticIPAddress event proves the host MAC was absent from that lease view; alarm mapping/action log proves enforcement was invoked; event absence does not prove the host is authorized if DHCP visibility is incomplete.
selected.remediation_path: Configure Access Point Management view, VLAN and IP ranges in Configuration Wizard; validate DHCP scope/relay and lease-file updates; map StaticIPAddress to an alarm/action; test both authorized DHCP and static-IP endpoints; use a VLAN-aware enforcement design when per-client isolation is required.
selected.question_fingerprint: Distinguish DHCP lease evidence from a VLAN enforcement mechanism; choose the correct interpretation of StaticIPAddress event and alarm mapping.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Non-VLAN-aware AP/hub with multiple clients on shared VLAN; DHCP lease-file validation branch; authorized lease versus missing lease event -> alarm/action.

selected.lesson_subject: Check Point VPN Integration in central mode: syslog session discovery, agent posture, and Smart-1 Cloud network-group enforcement
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F central-mode integration receives Check Point VPN login/logout syslog containing user ID, office-mode client IP, and group; initially places the client IP in a restricted network object group; agent posture scan determines compliance; Smart-1 Cloud REST API moves the IP to the unrestricted group on pass and returns it to restricted on logout.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: VPN client authenticates -> Check Point gateway creates office-mode session and sends syslog -> restricted object group keeps traffic isolated -> FortiNAC agent communicates over bidirectional TCP/4568 and reports posture -> FortiNAC updates Smart-1 Cloud groups through API -> user gets production access; logout syslog re-adds IP to restricted group.
selected.failure_class: Missing or stale Smart-1 Cloud API key; syslog source/port/format mismatch; office-mode IP pool or restricted/unrestricted group policy incorrect; agent TCP/4568 blocked; unsupported OS/iOS endpoint cannot run agent and remains isolated.
selected.evidence_pattern: Syslog event proves session discovery and supplies identity/IP/group; Smart-1 Cloud group membership proves enforcement state; agent scan result proves posture decision; successful VPN authentication alone does not prove production access was granted.
selected.remediation_path: Meet Check Point R81.10.10+ and FortiNAC-F 7.6.0+ requirements; configure remote-access VPN community, Smart-1 Cloud API key and URL, SNMP read/write access, syslog UDP/514 to primary and HA secondary, restricted/unrestricted groups and matching policy; allow bidirectional TCP/4568; validate login, posture pass, group move, and logout reversal.
selected.question_fingerprint: Trace the syslog -> restricted group -> agent posture -> Smart-1 Cloud group transition and identify which missing dependency leaves a VPN-authenticated user isolated.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Remote VPN endpoint -> Check Point gateway -> syslog to FortiNAC -> agent TCP/4568 posture -> Smart-1 Cloud API -> restricted/unrestricted network groups -> Check Point policy.

selected.lesson_subject: LDAP Service authentication-method selection: password-only versus all configured password and OTP factors
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.2+ LDAP Service General setting selects whether an LDAP bind verifies password only or all configured password and OTP factors; this is a server-side bind policy, distinct from RADIUS challenge handling and remote LDAP proxy behavior.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: LDAP client submits bind DN/credentials -> FortiAuthenticator resolves local LDAP user and configured factors -> password-only mode validates password and completes bind without OTP; all-factors mode requires configured OTP factor as part of bind authentication -> LDAP result returned to client.
selected.failure_class: LDAP client cannot provide interactive OTP but server is configured to require it; password-only mode unintentionally bypasses OTP for an application that assumes MFA; LDAP client test passes but downstream app authorization/group lookup still fails.
selected.evidence_pattern: LDAP bind result and FortiAuthenticator authentication logs show the selected factor path; LDAP client debug confirms bind success/failure; successful bind proves authentication for the configured LDAP service mode but does not prove downstream group/authorization mapping or MFA outside that bind.
selected.remediation_path: Inventory LDAP clients and their ability to supply OTP; select All configured password and OTP factors only where the client supports the required factor exchange; use Password-only only for a deliberately scoped integration with compensating controls; test both positive and negative binds and review logs after changing the global LDAP Service setting.
selected.question_fingerprint: Choose the bind-factor mode that matches the LDAP client's protocol capabilities and distinguish LDAP bind authentication from RADIUS Access-Challenge behavior.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: LDAP client bind request -> FortiAuthenticator LDAP Service -> password-only branch or password+OTP branch -> LDAP success/failure response; separate downstream authorization callout.

selected.lesson_subject: Kerberos authentication for native RDP Network Level Authentication: secret-derived realm and KDC discovery
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiPAM 1.9 native RDP launcher can use Kerberos for NLA; realm is constructed from the domain configured on the secret or target; KDC can be explicitly specified in Advanced Domain Settings or discovered through DNS SRV records; support is limited to the native RDP launcher.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: User launches native RDP through FortiPAM -> secret supplies target/domain credential context -> FortiPAM derives Kerberos realm -> resolve explicit KDC or DNS SRV -> obtain Kerberos ticket -> NLA authenticates before desktop session is established -> RDP session proceeds.
selected.failure_class: Target entered by IP instead of FQDN prevents SPN/realm alignment; secret domain differs from target domain; DNS SRV or KDC port 88 unreachable; NTLM fallback expectation conflicts with Kerberos-only policy; non-native launcher does not support this option.
selected.evidence_pattern: Secret RDP service shows NLA and Use Kerberos enabled; target KDC Address proves explicit KDC selection; DNS SRV resolution and KDC reachability prove discovery path; Kerberos ticket/KDC logs prove Kerberos exchange; successful TCP/3389 alone does not prove Kerberos was used.
selected.remediation_path: Use target FQDN and a Windows Domain Account secret or associate Target Only secret with the domain-account secret; enable RDP service and NLA plus Use Kerberos for NLA; set explicit KDC FQDN/port only when DNS SRV discovery is unsuitable; validate DNS, clock, SPN, KDC port 88, and native launcher support.
selected.question_fingerprint: Distinguish Kerberos NLA authentication from RDP transport forwarding; select the correct FQDN, realm, and KDC discovery remediation.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiPAM native RDP launcher -> secret/target realm -> DNS SRV or explicit KDC -> Kerberos ticket -> NLA gate -> Windows RDP session.

selected.lesson_subject: Raw Event Size licensing: GB/day metering, rolling violation window, and analytics lockout
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSIEM 7.2.2+ on-prem VM licensing measures total raw event size per day in GB, plus agent, UEBA-agent and FortiGuard IOC entitlements; it allows 11 violations in a rolling 30-day window, after which Dashboard and Analytics are disabled for one day.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Collectors ingest raw events -> daily raw event bytes are measured -> Admin > License > Usage records daily usage and violation state -> 11 rolling violations tolerated -> threshold exceeded disables Dashboard/Analytics for one day -> reduce/stop source forwarding or increase GB/day entitlement -> usage returns within entitlement and UI access recovers.
selected.failure_class: Daily raw event volume exceeds GB/day entitlement repeatedly; operators delete a CMDB device but its logs continue arriving; EPS/device counts are mistaken for the metered quantity; analytics lockout is mistaken for ingestion failure.
selected.evidence_pattern: Raw Event Usage chart shows red over-limit days; Top 10 devices and event types identify source volume; Collector/log arrival proves ingestion continues; UI access recovery after rolling violation count falls to 11 or below proves enforcement state, not that the source configuration is fixed.
selected.remediation_path: Inspect Admin > License > Usage > Raw event usage; select over-limit days and inspect Top 10 devices/event types; stop or reduce forwarding at the source/collector path (CMDB deletion alone is insufficient); verify daily GB stays under entitlement; if growth is expected, resize GB/day capacity with actual usage evidence.
selected.question_fingerprint: Differentiate GB/day from EPS/device count; identify why CMDB deletion does not stop ingestion; calculate the rolling 11-violation enforcement boundary.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Log sources -> Collector -> daily raw-event byte meter -> 30-day rolling violation counter -> Dashboard/Analytics access gate; remediation path back to compliant daily volume.

selected.lesson_subject: HTTP/3 (QUIC) inspection: agent/edge scope, SSL inspection action, and proxy-user fallback
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSASE can SSL-inspect HTTP/3 over QUIC without blocking QUIC for agent and edge-device traffic; the action is configured in a security profile group under SSL inspection; proxy-policy traffic is excluded and may require blocking UDP/443 at the endpoint to force HTTP/2/TLS 1.3 fallback.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiClient agent or edge device sends UDP/443 QUIC -> FortiSASE security profile group applies Inspect/Bypass/Block action -> Inspect enables SSL-dependent security profiles on HTTP/3; Bypass allows without SSL inspection; Block causes client to fall back to HTTP/2 in most cases; proxy-user path uses endpoint browser QUIC disablement when deep inspection is required.
selected.failure_class: Administrator expects proxy policy to inherit agent/edge QUIC inspection; SSL inspection method is not Certificate or Deep Inspection so HTTP/3 action is unavailable; endpoint continues QUIC after administrator blocks only TCP/443; inspection bypass mistaken for successful deep inspection.
selected.evidence_pattern: Security profile group shows configured HTTP/3 action and inspection method; agent/edge traffic logs show HTTP/3 classification; browser test to quic.nginx.org verifies QUIC behavior; proxy-policy logs are outside this setting and do not prove agent/edge action.
selected.remediation_path: Separate agent/edge and proxy traffic scopes; choose Certificate or Deep inspection before setting HTTP/3 action; use Inspect when SSL-dependent profiles must operate, Bypass only intentionally, or Block to force HTTP/2 fallback; for proxy users disable QUIC in supported browser settings and validate UDP/443 behavior.
selected.question_fingerprint: Select the correct action and traffic scope for agent/edge versus proxy users; distinguish QUIC block from TLS inspection and HTTP/2 fallback.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Three-path flow: agent/edge UDP/443 -> FortiSASE SSL inspection profile -> Inspect/Bypass/Block; separate proxy-user lane -> endpoint QUIC disable -> HTTP/2 fallback.

selected.lesson_subject: Bandwidth-threshold packet-duplication guard: overlay/underlay measurement and per-member shedding
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiOS 8.0 SD-WAN checks utilized upstream, downstream, or bidirectional bandwidth before duplicating packets; thresholds are configured per SD-WAN member in KB/s and measurement can use overlay or underlay bandwidth; duplication starts below threshold and stops above it.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Service rule/duplication policy selects packet -> SD-WAN member's configured threshold is evaluated against overlay or associated underlay usage -> if below threshold packet is duplicated to eligible overlays -> if above threshold duplication is suppressed on members sharing the constrained underlay -> when usage drops below threshold duplication resumes.
selected.failure_class: Duplication consumes scarce underlay bandwidth and worsens congestion; threshold set in wrong units/direction; underlay mode configured but overlays reference different physical members; operator assumes primary traffic is blocked when only duplicate copies are suppressed.
selected.evidence_pattern: `diagnose sys sdwan intf-sla-log <underlay>` reports used upstream/downstream/bidirectional bandwidth; packet capture or controlled ping shows duplicate copies on uncongested overlays and suppression on constrained ones; primary traffic continuity proves only duplicate shedding, not SLA health or path failover.
selected.remediation_path: Set the correct upstream/downstream/bidirectional threshold in KB/s; choose overlay or underlay measurement intentionally; map each overlay to the correct physical underlay; validate with controlled duplicated traffic and background load; tune threshold with headroom and monitor the correct interface.
selected.question_fingerprint: Interpret threshold direction/units and predict which overlays stop duplicating when they share an overloaded underlay; distinguish duplicate suppression from primary path failover.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Spoke with two physical underlays and four overlay tunnels; per-member threshold gates duplicate copies; high load on one underlay suppresses only its associated overlay duplicates while primary traffic continues.
